candidateSegments.teachingRole: Recognizable character moves its arms and legs while jumping; carry this visible question into independently implemented bone/skin explanation.

observed.before: Mario stands, then runs toward blocks.
observed.action: He jumps, bends/extends limbs, lands and jumps over a row of blocks.
observed.result: The whole character changes position while arms and legs also change pose.

claimLimits: Gameplay does not reveal bone matrices, vertex weights, runtime skinning method or bone counts.
Exclude long idle620–710, photo-mode471–477 and story capture sequence~760.

annotationPlan.target: Elbow/knee outlines only while visible; character is small, so use a same-time inset if needed, no freeze/slowdown.
annotationPlan.style: Short joint arcs / open surface contours and leader labels. No filled covering or invented engine bone/normal data.
annotationPlan.tracking: Follow verified screen motion; hide at occlusion/out-of-frame and clear at cut. Fine sample evidence is not per-frame tracking.
annotationPlan.captionClearance: Preserve source HUD and fixed lower-centre captions; use only meaningful focus, not constant full-body boxes.

candidateSegments.teachingRole: Different new source window from M21; shine a moving light across industrial plates, grooves and pipes, then compare geometry versus surface normal in our implementation.

observed.before: Dark industrial corridor with metal plates and pipes.
observed.action: Player sweeps flashlight while walking and turns across near surfaces.
observed.result: Small surface details brighten and darken within the moving beam.

claimLimits: Pixels alone cannot distinguish a particular groove made by geometry from a normal map.
Engine support for tangent-space normal mapping is independently documented in idSoftware source; no per-pixel renderer capture here.
Do not say turning normal mapping off in this clip: no such toggle is recorded.
